question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 1000 litres in 5 hours and 6 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 1800 litres?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Filling rate of **Pipe A** = 1000 / 5 = 200 litres/hr.

Filling rate of **Pipe B** = 1000 / 6 = 500/3 litres/hr.

Combined rate = 200 + 500/3 = (600 + 500) / 3 = 1100/3 litres/hr.

Time for 1800 litres = 1800 ÷ (1100/3) = (1800 × 3) / 1100 = 54/11 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 54/11 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Capacity for **Pipe A** (5 hrs) and **Pipe B** (6 hrs) = 1000 litres.

Target tank capacity = 1800 litres.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ If 30 units of work represents filling a 1000 litre tank.

⇒ Then for an 1800 litre tank, Work = (30 ÷ 1000) × 1800 = 3 × 18 = 54 units.

⇒ Combined Efficiency of **Pipe A + Pipe B** = 6 + 5 = 11 units/hr.

⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Time = 54 ÷ 11 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 54/11 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another fills it in y hours, both together fill it in (xy) / (x + y) hours for the same volume.

Inlet vs Outlet

Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while **outlet (leakage) pipes** have negative efficiency.

Work Proportion

If the volume to be filled changes, the total units of work in the **LCM method** must be scaled proportionally.</p
